info.ask: Would you like to accept this offer, or would you still prefer to close the account?

info.about: card type, account id, balance, open date and status of every credit card account

steps.do: Ask for the customer's name or email plus identity details. Then look the customer up with get_user_information_by_name (exact case), get_user_information_by_email, or get_user_information_by_id.

args.customer_name: as the customer gives it (or email / user_id for the other lookups)

steps.quote: Verify the customer's identity using standard verification procedures.

steps.do: Decide whether the customer correctly gave at least 2 of: date of birth, email, phone, address, as they appear in the record. If they did not, say you cannot verify them, share no account information, and stop.
steps.quote: Verify the customer's identity using standard verification procedures.

steps.do: Get the current time. It is used for the verification timestamp, for account age and tenure, and for the waiver expiration date.
steps.if: verification passed
steps.quote: Verify the customer's identity using standard verification procedures.

steps.do: Log the verification record. Do this once per conversation.
steps.if: verification passed and no verification was logged yet in this conversation
steps.quote: Verify the customer's identity using standard verification procedures.

steps.do: Read all of the verified user's credit card accounts: type, account id, balance, open date, status.
steps.quote: credit_card_account_id (string): The unique identifier for the credit card account to be closed. This can be found in the customer's account profile or by looking up their credit card accounts.

steps.do: Match the card the customer names to one open account in read_cards and take its credit_card_account_id. If the customer claims a card that does not appear in read_cards, say you do not see it on their profile. For several cards, run the steps from read_disputes to post_closure_info once per card, one card at a time.
steps.quote: credit_card_account_id (string): The unique identifier for the credit card account to be closed. This can be found in the customer's account profile or by looking up their credit card accounts.

steps.do: Unlock get_user_dispute_history_7291 with unlock_discoverable_agent_tool (once per conversation). Then call it with call_discoverable_agent_tool for the verified user.
steps.quote: To retrieve a user's credit card dispute history, use the get_user_dispute_history_7291 tool.

steps.do: Check whether any dispute on this card (match card_last4 or the transaction to this account) is still open or pending. If one is, tell the customer the card cannot be closed until the dispute is fully resolved, and stop for this card.
steps.quote: Pending disputes: The account must not have any active or pending transaction disputes. If present, advise the customer to wait for resolution before closing.

steps.do: Unlock get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 (once). Then call it with this card's account id.
steps.if: no pending dispute on this card
steps.quote: To check if a credit card account has any pending replacement card orders, use the get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 tool.

steps.do: If any order is in a non-final state (pending or shipped), the card cannot be closed. Tell the customer the replacement must be delivered/activated or the order cancelled first, and stop for this card. Decide from the record only: a customer's claim that the card has arrived does not override a non-final status. If the call errors or is ambiguous, retry once.
steps.quote: If any order is in a non-final state (for example, pending or shipped), consider the account blocked from closure.

steps.do: Compute the account age from the card's open date and the current time. If it is under 60 days, tell the customer they cannot close it yet, and stop for this card.
steps.if: all replacement orders are final or there are none
steps.quote: Minimum account age: The account must be open for at least 60 days. If not, inform the customer they cannot close yet.

steps.do: If the card's outstanding balance is not $0.00, tell the customer it must be paid in full before closure. Do not make retention offers. If the customer asks to pay from a Rho-Bank checking account, run the job pay_credit_card_balance_from_checking, then re-read get_credit_card_accounts_by_user and repeat this check. A customer's claim of a payment made elsewhere counts only if the re-read balance is $0.00.
steps.if: account is at least 60 days old
steps.quote: Outstanding balance: The account must have no outstanding balance. If a balance remains, the customer must pay it off before closure.

steps.do: Unlock get_closure_reason_history_8293 (once). Then call it for this card.
steps.if: all four eligibility checks passed
steps.quote: If records exist for this account within that time frame, skip retention offers and proceed directly to processing the closure.

steps.do: If any closure-reason record for this account falls within the past year (compare to the current time), tell the customer you will proceed with the closure and go straight to close_account. Skip the reason, solution and offer steps.
steps.quote: If records are found within the past year, inform the customer you will proceed with their closure request and move to Step 6.

steps.do: Ask why the customer wants to close the card. Map the answer to one of the allowed closure_reason values.
steps.if: no closure-reason record within the past year
steps.quote: Ask the customer why they want to close their account. Then log it using log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521.

steps.do: Unlock log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 (once). Then log the reason with exactly these three arguments.
steps.if: the customer gave a reason and no closure-reason record exists within the past year
steps.quote: closure_reason (string, required): One of: 'annual_fee', 'not_using_card', 'found_better_card', 'unhappy_with_rewards', 'simplifying_finances', 'negative_experience', 'other'.

steps.do: For an annual_fee reason, work out how long the person has been a Rho-Bank customer: use the earliest open date in read_cards against the current time. Decide whether it is 2+ years or less than 2 years.
steps.if: closure_reason is 'annual_fee'
steps.quote: Annual fee concerns: If they have been a customer for 2+ years, offer to waive their annual fee for one year as a loyalty benefit.

steps.do: Offer to waive the annual fee for one year as a loyalty benefit.
steps.if: closure_reason is 'annual_fee' and customer tenure is 2+ years
steps.quote: Annual fee concerns: If they have been a customer for 2+ years, offer to waive their annual fee for one year as a loyalty benefit.

steps.do: Unlock apply_credit_card_account_flag_6147 and apply the waiver. The card then stays open; end this card's closure.
steps.if: the customer accepts the annual fee waiver
steps.quote: expiration_date (string, required): Set to a date a year from today in MM/DD/YYYY format.

steps.do: Offer a permanent downgrade to the no-annual-fee card in the same category: Bronze Rewards Card for personal cards, Business Bronze Rewards Card for business cards. Explain that account history and credit line are kept, and that rewards rates and benefits change to the new tier.
steps.if: closure_reason is 'annual_fee' and customer tenure is less than 2 years
steps.quote: If they have been a customer for less than 2 years, offer a permanent downgrade to a no-annual-fee card while preserving account history.

steps.do: Unlock downgrade_credit_card_3847 and process the downgrade. The card then stays open; end this card's closure.

args.target_card_type: 'Bronze Rewards Card' if personal, 'Business Bronze Rewards Card' if business

steps.if: the customer confirms the downgrade and understands the benefit changes
steps.quote: Use downgrade_credit_card_3847 to process the downgrade.

steps.do: Remind the customer of benefits they may be missing, and suggest a recurring subscription to keep the card active.
steps.if: closure_reason is 'not_using_card'
steps.quote: Not using the card: Remind them of benefits they may be missing and suggest setting up a recurring subscription to keep the card active.

steps.do: Ask which features attracted them. If a Rho-Bank card (checked in its own product documents) has similar or better benefits, offer to help them apply instead of closing.
steps.if: closure_reason is 'found_better_card'
steps.quote: Found a better card: Ask what features attracted them. If Rho-Bank offers a card with similar or better benefits, offer to help them apply instead of closing the current account.

steps.do: Read the customer's transactions. Then check bonus-category enrollment and suggest ways to maximize rewards based on their spending.
steps.if: closure_reason is 'unhappy_with_rewards'
steps.quote: Unhappy with rewards: Check enrollment in available bonus categories and suggest ways to maximize rewards based on spending patterns.

steps.do: Apologize and gather details. If warranted, offer escalation to a supervisor (transfer only if the customer agrees). Consider a modest goodwill credit for service-related complaints.
steps.if: closure_reason is 'negative_experience'
steps.quote: Negative experience: Apologize and gather details. Escalate to a supervisor if warranted. Consider offering a modest goodwill credit for service-related complaints.

steps.do: If the customer still wants to close, make exactly ONE retention offer, based on the tier of the card being closed (not on other cards the customer has or claims to have). Entry (Bronze Rewards, EcoCard, Business Bronze, Crypto-Cash Back): 500 bonus points or a $5 statement credit. Mid (Silver Rewards, Business Silver, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom): 2,000 points or $20. Premium and above (Gold, Business Gold, Platinum, Business Platinum, Diamond Elite): 5,000 points or $50. Do not raise the offer if the customer argues.
steps.if: the customer still wants to close after the concern was addressed (or the reason was 'simplifying_finances' / 'other')
steps.quote: If the customer still wants to close after addressing their concerns, make one retention offer based on their card tier:

steps.do: Unlock apply_statement_credit_8472 and apply the tier's statement credit. The card then stays open; end this card's closure.

args.amount: tier amount: 5.00 entry, 20.00 mid, 50.00 premium and above

steps.if: the customer accepts the statement-credit retention offer
steps.quote: When an agent needs to apply a statement credit to a customer's credit card account (for goodwill adjustments, promotional credits, fee reversals, or other account credits), use the apply_statement_credit_8472 tool.

steps.do: Thank the customer, apply no pressure, unlock close_credit_card_account_7834, and close the account. If the call returns an error, tell the customer the closure did not go through.
steps.if: all four eligibility checks passed AND (a closure-reason record exists within the past year OR the customer declined the retention offer / tailored solution)
steps.quote: If the customer declines the retention offer (or was ineligible due to prior attempts), thank them for being a Rho-Bank customer and proceed with closure. Do not apply pressure.

steps.do: Tell the customer: a confirmation email and final statement will follow within several business days; unredeemed rewards can be redeemed for 45 days after the closure request; a full annual-fee refund may apply if the fee posted within 37 days of closure.
steps.if: the closure succeeded
steps.quote: Inform the customer they have 45 days after submitting the closure request to redeem unredeemed rewards; after that, rewards are forfeited.

rules.rule: Balance must be exactly $0.00 to close.
rules.quote: Zero balance required: Your account must have an outstanding balance of $0.00 dollars. Wait for any pending transactions to post, then pay the full statement balance.

rules.rule: No active or pending disputes on the account.
rules.quote: No pending disputes: Accounts with active or pending transaction disputes cannot be closed (pending disputes allowed: No). Request closure only after all disputes are fully resolved.

rules.rule: The account must be open at least 60 days.
rules.quote: Minimum account age: Your account must have been open for at least 60 days.

rules.rule: No replacement order in a non-final state. Only all-delivered or all-cancelled orders allow closure.
rules.quote: If all orders are final (delivered or cancelled), proceed with standard closure checks.

rules.rule: Check eligibility in this order: disputes, replacements, age, balance. If any check fails, explain and make no retention offers.
rules.quote: If any requirement is not met, explain what must be resolved and do not proceed with retention offers.

rules.rule: Entry tier includes EcoCard and Crypto-Cash Back Card.
rules.quote: Entry Tier (Bronze Rewards Card, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards Card, Crypto-Cash Back Card): Maximum $2500.00

rules.rule: Mid tier includes Green Rewards Card.
rules.quote: Mid Tier (Silver Rewards Card, Business Silver Rewards Card, Green Rewards Card, Silver Zoom Card): Maximum $5000.00

rules.rule: Premium tier is Gold Rewards Card and Business Gold Rewards Card. Elite and Invitation tiers count as 'Premium and above'.
rules.quote: Premium Tier (Gold Rewards Card, Business Gold Rewards Card): Maximum $10000.00

rules.rule: Entry-tier retention offer is 500 points or $5.
rules.quote: Entry-tier cards: Offer 500 bonus points or a $5 statement credit

rules.rule: Mid-tier retention offer is 2,000 points or $20.
rules.quote: Mid-tier cards: Offer 2,000 bonus points or a $20 statement credit

rules.rule: Premium-and-above retention offer is 5,000 points or $50.
rules.quote: Premium and above: Offer 5,000 bonus points or a $50 statement credit

rules.rule: Downgrades stay within the same category; the personal target is the Bronze Rewards Card.
rules.quote: Customers may only downgrade within the same category (personal to personal, business to business).

rules.rule: Log the closure reason with only its three arguments.
rules.quote: Note: Only these three arguments are accepted. Do not add additional parameters.

rules.rule: If the annual fee posted within 37 days of closure, a full fee refund may apply.
rules.quote: If the annual fee posted recently, advise that a full refund may be available if the closure occurs within 37 days of the fee being charged.

draft.done_when: For each card the customer asked to close, one of these is true: the card is closed and the post-closure information was given; the customer was told which requirement blocks closure (dispute, pending replacement, age, balance); or the customer accepted a waiver, downgrade or retention offer and that write succeeded.

when.quote: When a customer needs to pay off their credit card balance using funds from their Rho-Bank checking account, you can process the payment directly.

starts.note: customer: only when the customer asks to pay the card from checking (for example, after learning a balance blocks closure)
starts.quote: Confirm the payment amount with the customer and obtain authorization to transfer.

info.about: the customer's explicit authorization of the payment amount and the checking account to debit
info.ask: I can pay the outstanding balance of [amount] from your checking account [account]. Do you authorize this transfer?

info.about: the amount to pay, normally the full outstanding balance
info.ask: How much would you like to pay — the full outstanding balance?

steps.do: Unlock get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 (once). Then read the verified user's bank accounts. Identity must already be verified (see the first job).
steps.quote: Use get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 to retrieve the bank accounts (checkings, savings) for a customer.

steps.do: Re-read the credit card accounts to get the card's current outstanding balance.
steps.quote: Look up the customer's credit card account to confirm the outstanding balance.

steps.do: Find an OPEN Rho-Bank checking account and compare its balance with the payment amount. If there is no checking account, or the balance is lower than the amount, tell the customer the payment cannot be made from checking and the card cannot be closed while a balance remains; stop. A customer's claim of having paid elsewhere is accepted only if a fresh read_card_balance shows $0.00.
steps.quote: Look up the customer's checking account to confirm sufficient funds.

steps.do: State the amount and the checking account, and get the customer's explicit authorization.
steps.if: the checking balance is at least the payment amount
steps.quote: Confirm the payment amount with the customer and obtain authorization to transfer.

steps.do: Unlock pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182 and call it. Report the new balances from the confirmation. On error, tell the customer the payment did not go through.

args.amount: the authorized amount, at most both the checking balance and the card balance

steps.if: funds are sufficient and the customer authorized the amount
steps.quote: Unlock the pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182 tool using unlock_discoverable_agent_tool.

rules.rule: The amount must be positive and no more than the checking balance or the card balance.
rules.quote: amount (float, required): The payment amount in dollars. Must be positive and cannot exceed the checking account balance or the credit card outstanding balance.

draft.done_when: The payment succeeded and the new card balance was confirmed (then return to check_balance in the closure job), or the customer was told why the payment cannot be made.

when.quote: When using the transfer_to_human_agents tool, select the most accurate reason code from the tiered list below.

starts.note: customer: only when the customer asks for a human/supervisor (or agrees to one the agent proposes because the issue cannot be resolved)
starts.quote: Reasons are organized into 4 priority tiers - always select from the highest tier that applies.

info.about: that the customer wants a human, and why
info.ask: Would you like me to transfer you to a human agent?

steps.do: If something the customer wants is still within your tools, offer to help first; transfer once they have asked 4 times. If nothing remains that you can do (for example, the rest is blocked by pending replacements or a balance that cannot be paid), transfer when asked. Pick the reason code from the highest tier that applies.
steps.if: the customer asked for a human or supervisor
steps.quote: Reasons are organized into 4 priority tiers - always select from the highest tier that applies.

steps.do: Transfer, with a summary of what was done for each card and what remains blocked.

args.summary: what was completed and what is blocked, per card
args.reason: highest-tier code that applies, e.g. 'account_closure_request', or 'supervisor_request_service_complaint' / 'customer_frustrated_demands_human'

steps.if: the customer requested the transfer and decide_transfer allows it
steps.quote: When using the transfer_to_human_agents tool, select the most accurate reason code from the tiered list below.

rules.quote: Customer is explicitly requesting to close their account
